Based on the provided text, here is a summary of **US Constitution (1870)**, covering pages 1–9:

*   **[1] Bicameral Legislature:** The document establishes a bicameral legislature with a House of Representatives (members chosen every two years) and a Senate (six-year terms with staggered vacancies).
*   **[2] Legislative Powers & President's Role:** All legislative powers are vested in Congress, which must present bills to the President for approval before becoming law; if not signed within ten days, they take effect unless Congress adjourns. Joint consent orders require presidential approval and a two-thirds supermajority override.
*   **[3] Executive Powers & Judicial Structure:** Executive power rests with an elected four-year President (Commander-in-Chief) appointed by the Senate; compensation cannot be altered during the term, and removal requires impeachment. The judicial power is vested in a supreme court established by Congress to handle cases involving ambassadors, maritime disputes, and state/citizen controversies.
*   **[4] Legal Supremacy & Ratification:** The Constitution is the supreme law of the land, overriding state laws and treaties; all pre-adoption debts remain valid under this framework; ratification requires unanimous consent from nine states.

*Summary of all 9 pages.*
